elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both Parties.
elements.evidence: Subsection (b) limits the total liability “for either Party,” establishing a mutual cap.

elements.element: The fee-based cap limb equals fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: Subsection (b) uses “fees paid or payable by IBM under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim.”

elements.element: The cap is no less than USD 1,000,000 through a greater-of formulation.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no USD 1,000,000 floor or greater-of formulation.

elements.element: Indirect damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: Subsection (a) is mutual but does not exclude indirect damages generally; listing consequential and incidental damages does not expressly cover all indirect damages.

elements.element: Consequential damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: Subsection (a) provides that neither Party is liable to the other for consequential damages.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Subsection (c) states that the cap in Subsection 15.3(b) does not apply to a Party’s breach of its confidentiality obligations.

elements.element: Liability for breach of data protection obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No carve-out addresses data protection obligations, and they are not demonstrably coextensive with confidentiality obligations.

elements.element: Liability for breach of security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No carve-out addresses security obligations.

elements.element: Indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: Subsection (c) expressly excludes a Party’s indemnification obligations from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Subsection (c) expressly excludes gross negligence from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for wilful misconduct is uncapped.

elements.element: Liability for fraud is uncapped.

result.reason: The redline fully reaches the fallback: it creates a mutual twelve-month-fees cap and includes all four required uncapped carve-outs. It does not reach the preferred position because it omits the USD 1,000,000 floor, a general indirect-damages exclusion, several required carve-outs, and the payment-obligations clarification. The changes are substantively targeted and preserve the existing mutual damages exclusion, but drafting quality is materially reduced by the visible doubled punctuation and an unresolved/misleading cross-reference to “Subsection 15.3(b)” where the rendered clause itself is only labeled “b),” making the carve-out’s operative target uncertain on the face of the supplied text.
